issue.title: docs/capture.md marker table still calls `Title @dir/stem` reserved/refused; it is a shipped existing-record update
issue.description:
The marker table near the top of `docs/capture.md` (line 107 at `70f69c23`) still says:

| `Title @dir/stem` | Reserved: refused until capture can append to an existing note |

That has been wrong since `12641768` ("feat(capture): parse existing record updates"): `@dir/stem` without a caret is a working existing-record update (`capture-parse` mode `record_update`). The same file's `### Record notes` section, `docs/reference/capture-syntax.md` (`@dir/` / `@dir/^stem` / `@dir/stem` → "Record create, explicit stem, or existing-record update"), and `docs/records.md` all describe the shipped behavior correctly, so only this one row is stale.

Root cause: the row was written when grammar 20 reserved the spelling and was not updated when updates shipped.

Fix: reword the row to match the Record notes section, e.g. `Title @dir/stem` → "Update an existing Record Note: append notes, change supplied fields (see [Record notes](#record-notes))". Check for any other "Reserved" wording for `@dir/stem` in docs/ while there.

Found while researching why `@album/^stem` needs the caret (research:202611/record_stem_caret_rationale.md).

task_type_fields.impact: Docs-only: readers (and agents) are told @dir/stem is refused and may avoid record updates or misexplain the ^ in @dir/^stem.
task_type_fields.repro: grep -n 'Reserved: refused until' docs/capture.md  → row says @dir/stem is refused; but `bob capture-parse 'Revisited @eat/ninja_sushi'` reports mode record_update (and @eat/ninja_suhsi gives record_not_found with a did-you-mean), proving updates ship.

issue.creation_reason: Found during caret-syntax research: one docs row contradicts shipped behavior and the rest of the docs, which misleads readers about record updates.
